turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes, and I'd like to know why my son found out about a zero from his phone in the middle of class.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
Meredith is fine. Now, who decided to enter that zero, and was anyone going to speak to Owen before they did?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.
A machine's guess. The company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student, and your own procedure says the same. So what else do you have, or is that it?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.
"Quite reliable." Okay. Fourteen detection tools were tested last year and the researchers called them neither accurate nor reliable, so I'm asking again: what else do you have besides a number?
So I had to give him a zero.
"Had to." Under which rule? Procedure 4.2 says you call the parent before any mark goes in, and 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish a concern. So you decided first and asked questions later.
I hope you understand my position.
"Hope." Okay. My position is that my son was punished by a number nobody checked, so withdraw the zero and tell me what you actually have.
